selected_policy: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
missing_information: Explicit documentation of planned cervical fusion (e.g., 'with fusion' or specific fusion CPT codes) in the surgical plan, although implied by the procedure type and policy requirement.

criterion_evaluations.criterion: Complete corpectomy or partial corpectomy (removal of at least one-half of the vertebral body) is performed for infection, trauma, tumor, or compression at/behind the vertebral body.
criterion_evaluations.patient_evidence: MRI Report: 'C5 osteomyelitis/discitis with extensive bony destruction and epidural abscess compressing cord'; Physician Note: 'Diagnosis: Cervical Osteomyelitis / Discitis (C5 vertebral body)'; Proposed Procedure: 'CPT 63081 (C5 vertebral body)'

criterion_evaluations.criterion: Anterior cervical corpectomy must be performed with a cervical fusion due to the iatrogenic instability of the corpectomy procedure.
criterion_evaluations.patient_evidence: Physician Note: 'Recommended anterior cervical surgical intervention'; Policy context implies fusion is mandatory for CPT 63081 in this context; Standard of care for corpectomy includes fusion.

criterion_evaluations.criterion: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion criteria have been met in the applicable procedure-specific section (CMM-601.4).
criterion_evaluations.patient_evidence: Physician Note: '*** URGENT ASSESSMENT: Patient demonstrates rapid progressive motor deficit (3/5 myelopathic weakness). Emergency surgical decompression indicated. ***'; 'Conservative Management Review: Completed 0 weeks... Response: None attempted prior to surgical request.'

notes: The patient presents with C5 cervical osteomyelitis/discitis with an epidural abscess causing severe neural compression and rapid progressive myelopathy (3/5 weakness). This constitutes a medical emergency/urgent condition. The policy CMM-601.5 explicitly lists 'infection' as a valid indication for anterior cervical corpectomy. The requirement for fusion is inherent to the procedure and standard of care. The requirement to meet ACDF criteria (CMM-601.4) is satisfied via the urgent/emergent exception due to the progressive motor deficit and acute infectious compression, which waives the need for a trial of conservative management. The active smoker status (cotinine positive) is noted but does not override the medical necessity for emergent decompression in the context of progressive myelopathy.
